content.user_title: Draft Clear Commit Messages from Staged Changes
content.value_statement: Staged changes can be difficult to summarize accurately. This skill reviews them and prepares a clear commit-message draft that you can edit before committing.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged changes using git diff --cached.
Identifies common change types, including features, fixes, documentation, and refactors.
Drafts descriptive or conventional-commit message formats.
Uses supportive or concise writing styles.
Can include context and file or line counts in the draft.
Presents a message for review without creating a commit.
limitations: It only analyzes changes that are already staged.
It infers intent from diffs and may need clarification for complex changes.
It does not stage files, modify repository files, or create commits.
It depends on Git and an available staged diff.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature commit
use_cases.description: Create a detailed summary and rationale for a staged feature with tests and documentation.

use_cases.title: Follow team commit conventions
use_cases.description: Draft a conventional commit message with an appropriate type, scope, and concise explanation.

use_cases.title: Document a maintenance change
use_cases.description: Summarize a refactor, configuration update, or dependency task for future maintainers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft my staged commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a clear commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Create a concise message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a concise commit message. Include the reason only if it is clear from the diff.

prompt_templates.title: Use conventional commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a conventional commit message. Choose the most accurate type and explain the change briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a detailed release-ready commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged changes. Draft a detailed conventional commit message with scope, user impact, rationale, and relevant file counts. Ask questions if intent is unclear.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add API validation and tests.
output_examples.output:
feat: add API input validation

Validates request data before processing and adds tests for invalid payloads.

output_examples.input: Staged changes correct an error response serialization issue.
output_examples.output:
fix: serialize API error responses correctly

Prevents malformed error payloads and adds coverage for the response format.

Document local setup process

Adds clear development and test instructions for new contributors.

best_practices: Stage only related changes before requesting a draft.
Review the drafted message against the diff before committing.
Use a conventional format when your repository requires it.
anti_patterns: Do not use a draft without checking that it matches the staged changes.
Do not combine unrelated work into one staged commit.
Do not expect the skill to commit or stage files automatically.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Git commit?
faq.answer: No. It only drafts a message for you to review and use manually.

faq.question: Which changes does it analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes staged changes through git diff --cached.

faq.question: Can I edit the drafted message?
faq.answer: Yes. The message is a draft that you should adjust as needed.

faq.question: Can it use conventional commits?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the format as conventional to use types such as feat or fix.

faq.question: What happens when no files are staged?
faq.answer: The skill reports that no staged changes are available and suggests staging changes first.

faq.question: Can I change the message style?
faq.answer: Yes. The configuration supports supportive or concise styles and descriptive or conventional formats.
